verdicts.evidence: Numerical experiments on 45 instances show the transformed objective is non-linear (chord gap [1.037e-4, 8.139e-2]) while untransformed E_π[r] is exactly linear (2.22e-16); multi-criterion adaptation tested on 60 instances with IAMA outperforming naive in 60/60 cases; mutation (N=1) collapses non-linearity as predicted.

Functional derivative matches finite differences (max rel error 7.33e-8 over 80 cases); drop-in replacement on standard GRPO reaches true optimum (max suboptimality 5.55e-16 over 30 instances); empirical π̂ convergence slope −1.024 vs theory −1; mutation with plain reward is strictly worse in 30/30 cases.

2250 bound evaluations across 90 instances show 0 violations above 1e-12; max excess loss at T=25 is 2.04e-6; mutation with wrong step size (η=20/L) yields 11 macroscopic violations and mutation with plain reward yields 36/36 violations, confirming theorem conditions.

Full bound never violated over 60 configs × 200 runs with max LHS/RHS ratio 0.2611; ε and δ measured from actual iterates; dropping the 2(ε+δ)/β term causes violations in 36/36 noisy configs (max ratio 1.65e10); plateau grows monotonically with noise in 12/12 cells.

Sympy confirms the CDF integrates to 1; first-order optimality at claimed π* holds to machine precision (span ≤5.84e-16 for all N); naive optimum puts mass 1.0 at y≈0.5 (δ_0.5 collapse) vs IAMA N=8 with 0.922 mass outside [0.25,0.75]; mutations confirm α=1/(N−1) is the correct exponent.

No experiments were executed; blockers include GPU-scale 7B GRPO training, unreleased author-trained reward models and judges, no public code, and figure-only evidence with no numeric table to re-assert.

overall: The logbook provides thorough numerical verification of the paper's five mathematical claims (objective formulation, algorithm, two convergence theorems, and the bimodal-policy proposition) using synthetic reward functions, multiple seeds, mutation tests, and independent solvers. The sole empirical LLM claim (HH-RLHF/Alpaca-7B Pareto front) is not addressed at all due to GPU scale and unreleased model dependencies.
